newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: EBRD CONSIDERING STAKE IN CZECH AGROBANKA - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: EBRD CONSIDERING STAKE IN CZECH AGROBANKA - PAPER.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is considering taking a 10-20 percent stake in troubled Czech bank Agrobanka, the economic daily Hospodarske Noviny reported on Thursday.

The paper quoted EBRD Czech Team Leader Jiri Huebner as saying the central bank had approached the EBRD about taking a stake in the bank, but that the London-based institution would be interested only in a minority stake of "10-20 percent".
"(And) only in the case that Agrobanka will have a trustworthy partner with a clear business strategy," the paper quoted Huebner as saying.

On Tuesday the central bank placed Agrobanka under temporary forced administration after it experienced liquidity problems arising from the failure of Kreditni Banka Plzen a.s. and the investigation of people in the Kreditni case who are also connected to Agrobanka.

The central bank, in its 12th intervention into a commercial bank in the post-Communist period, said it would guarantee all of Agrobanka's obligations during the forced administration period of an unspecified duration.
In addition, CNB Governor Josef Tosovsky instructed the "big banks" to prepare up to six billion crowns to help liquidity at Agrobanka.
Agrobanka is the largest wholly-private Czech bank with basic capital of some four billion crowns at the end of last year.
